title: Helios Financial - Incident Postmortem & Mitigations
summary: Follow-up on the April 14th incident that caused elevated latency and partial degradation for Helios' risk scoring pipeline. Reviewed root cause (serve autoscaler misconfiguration + degraded KV cache), mitigations deployed, short-term mitigation plan, and proposed reliability improvements including better autoscaler policies, cache warm-up, and runbook updates.
next_steps: Redwood to share revised autoscaling policy and playbook by 2026-04-24
Helios to provide logs from the failed pod (namespace: risk-prod) by 2026-04-23
Schedule canary run for new config week of 2026-04-27
Redwood SE to run a targeted KV-cache benchmark with Helios payloads and share results
action_items: Samir Patel: Produce autoscaler policy diff and recommended thresholds; due 2026-04-24
Maya Turner: Upload namespace risk-prod logs to shared S3; due 2026-04-23
Jordan Cruz: Send security compliance packet and SOC2 artifacts link; due 2026-04-23
Liam O'Connor: Coordinate canary window and invite Redwood; due 2026-04-26
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Avery Lin (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Jordan Cruz (Redwood CSM); Maya Turner, Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair, Nora Weiss (Helios)

Summary: quick follow-up after the April 14th outage, walk through what happened and what we did, and agree next steps.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight 45 minutes ish. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Maya: maya here, head of platform at helios, thanks for doing this, we want concrete fixes and dates
[00:15] Liam: liam S-R-E, i ran the oncall that night, happy to dig into logs
[00:20] Priya: priya security, a few compliance questions later
[00:25] Avery: great, samir do you want to kick off with timeline and RCA?
[00:30] Samir: yeah sure. so timeline first, approx 02:10 UTC on april 14th the risk scoring pipeline experienced increased tail latency, and by 02:18 we hit our fallback policy, some requests started to misroute to the lower-capacity variant. around 02:22 a subset of inference pods OOM'd during KV cache rebuild, this is important — the K-V cash, sorry — the KV cache warm-up ended up filling memory under our current GC/eviction settings.
[00:55] Nora: when you say misroute is that the 'redwood dedicate' variant or a regional fallback?
[01:02] Samir: good q. misroute was to the dedicated-lite variant we have as a fallback for cost tiering. not a region fallback. the routing policy triggered because the autoscaler temporarily returned fewer replicas due to a spurious monitoring spike.
[01:18] Liam: to be clear, our autoscaler dropped us from 12 to 6 replicas in about 90s, which gave the system no time to rebuild the KV cache gracefully.
[01:25] Samir: yep, that matches our logs. the scale-down policy had a cooldown that was too aggressive for this workload. also one of the host machines had a transient NVMe error that delayed pod restarts, compounding the problem.
[01:40] Maya: did we see any data exposure? priya?
[01:44] Priya: we did a quick audit, looks like no exfil. tokens are encrypted with K-M-S and audit logs stamped. but we need the full audit log export for legal.
[01:55] Jordan: we've uploaded preliminary logs to the shared folder link: https://redwood.app/helios/incident-logs (redwood internal link)
[02:03] Avery: ok noted. Samir, walk us through mitigations you pushed that night.
[02:08] Samir: short term we rolled back to the previous autoscaler policy (the conservative one), increased pod memory limit by 25% on the affected service, and disabled immediate scale-down triggers for 5 minutes windows. also we applied a KV cache warm-up step during startup to avoid rebuild spikes.
[02:28] Liam: that helped, we saw tail latency drop within 10 minutes of the rollback.
[02:33] Maya: appreciate that. what's the plan to prevent recurrence?
[02:37] Samir: long-term recommendations:
- adjust scale-down threshold to consider in-flight KV state
- implement graceful cache eviction and incremental warm-up so not all pods rebuild simultaneously
- host health checks to avoid scheduling on hosts with transient NVMe errors
- add a canary/rolling window during config changes with traffic shaping
[03:00] Nora: can you quantify risk / RTO if this happens again?
[03:04] Samir: if left unchanged we'd expect 5-8% of requests to fallback for a 10-20 minute window under similar spike patterns. with our recommended changes that drops to under 1% and <2 minutes of elevated latency for a worst-case node loss.
[03:18] Priya: for compliance, what logs do you keep and for how long? we need 1 year of audit trail for SAS-3 internal control, and retention policies need to be shown.
[03:29] Jordan: Redwood keeps request and audit logs for 90 days by default; enterprise retention add-on can do 12 months, we will share the retention contract. I'll attach SOC2, ISO docs in the packet.
[03:40] Maya: ok send that. also our legal team requested the change history and who approved the autoscaler policy that was live in prod.
[03:47] Avery: we can export the config change history from the console, samir will pull the PRs and approvals.
[03:53] Liam: also we saw a couple of confusing metrics in the console — some of the token-level latency charts looked misaligned with our ingested metrics. any known clock drift?
[04:02] Samir: there was a short-lived metric delay because our metric pipeline to the console uses batched flushes; not clock drift but ingestion latency. we've raised the ingestion frequency for the risk-prod dashboard.
[04:14] Nora: thanks. about the KV cache warm-up, you mentioned incremental warm-up — how does that interact with canary?
[04:20] Samir: incremental warm-up means pods restore prefixes progressively and serve cold misses to a small, throttled queue while metrics confirm readiness. for canary we'd do the canary replica set with warm-up enabled but limited traffic (10-15%) and monitor cache hit rate, miss latencies.
[04:35] Maya: great. how long before you can share the autoscaler diff and a playbook we can run?
[04:40] Samir: we'll have a diff and playbook draft by 2026-04-24.
[04:44] Jordan: and security packet by 2026-04-23, including SOC2 artifact links.
[04:48] Priya: on encryption — KMS key rotation, are customer keys supported?
[04:52] Avery: yes, customer-managed keys are supported for dedicated and private customers; for hosted we offer a managed KMS with export controls. we'll send the KMS integration guide.
[04:59] Liam: last technical Q: could quantization have contributed? we run an int8 variant in prod for cost, could that cause instability under rebuilds?
[05:06] Samir: quantization changes shouldn't cause OOMs during KV cache rebuilds; it's more memory allocation patterns. but we'll include a note in the bench results. we will run a targeted bench with Helios' payload and the int8 variant.
[05:17] Maya: ok let's talk escalation posture — if this happens again we need an automated rollback and paged incident leads. can you add a runbook step?
[05:24] Jordan: agreed, adding a postmortem checklist and automatic rollback trigger based on combined signals (tail latency + cache miss) is on our runbook draft.
[05:32] Avery: cool. next steps recap?
[05:36] Samir: samir will send autoscaler policy diff + playbook by 4/24
[05:40] Jordan: jordan will send security packet + SOC2 links by 4/23
[05:43] Maya: maya will upload logs by 4/23
[05:47] Liam: liam to set up canary window for week of 4/27 and invite you
[05:50] Priya: priya to confirm KMS questions after review of packet
[05:55] Avery: thanks all — we'll follow up in the thread, and we'll schedule a canary kickoff once logs and configs are shared.
[05:59] (end)
